syllabusTopics: Saturated hydrocarbons (Alkanes): preparation from haloalkanes (reduction and Wurtz reaction), decarboxylation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkene and alkyne
Chemical properties of alkanes: substitution reactions (halogenation, nitration and sulphonation only), oxidation of ethane
Unsaturated hydrocarbons (Alkenes): preparation by dehydration of alcohol, dehydrohalogenation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkyne
Chemical properties of alkenes: addition reaction with HX (Markovnikov's addition and peroxide effect), H2O, O3, H2SO4 only
Alkynes: preparation from carbon and hydrogen, 1,2-dibromoethane, chloroform/iodoform only
Chemical properties of alkynes: addition reaction with H2, HX, H2O; acidic nature (action with sodium, ammoniacal AgNO3 and ammoniacal Cu2Cl2)
Test of unsaturation (ethene and ethyne): bromine water test and Baeyer's test
Comparative studies of physical properties of alkane, alkene and alkyne
Kolbe's electrolysis methods for the preparation of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes

card.title: Markovnikov's rule — the rich get richer (in H)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Alkanes substitute (free-radical halogenation), alkenes/alkynes ADD across the π bond. Markovnikov: the H of HX lands on the already H-rich carbon, via the more stable carbocation (3° > 2° > 1°) — peroxides flip it for HBr only (Kharasch/anti-Markovnikov). Terminal alkynes are weakly acidic (≡C–H + Na/ammoniacal Ag⁺/Cu⁺ salts). Brown bromine water and purple Baeyer's reagent both bleach at unsaturation.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Markovnikov: H→H-rich C, X→H-poor C (stable carbocation path)  ·  peroxide effect: HBr ONLY, reversed  ·  ethene + H₂/Ni → ethane  ·  but-2-ene + O₃/Zn,H₂O → 2 CH₃CHO (double bond location proof)  ·  acetylene + 2[Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ → Ag–C≡C–Ag↓ (white) + …

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Markovnikov needs an unsymmetrical alkene + ionic (non-peroxide) HX addition. Peroxide reversal is HBr-specific (HCl/HI stay Markovnikov — bond-strength energetics). Catalytic hydrogenation needs Ni/Pt/Pd surface; Baeyer's stays alkaline and cold or it over-oxidises.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Ethene → ethane by H₂/Ni (NEB 2023, mechanism = surface adsorption, syn-addition). But-2-ene ozonolysis gives 2 ethanal — cleavage products map the old double bond (NEB 2022). Wurtz couples 2RX + 2Na → R–R (symmetrical alkanes best); Kolbe electrolyses RCOONa → R–R at the anode.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Ethane from ethene: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ →(Ni, heat) CH₃–CH₃ — H₂ adsorbs dissociatively on nickel, both H add syn to the π bond (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Ozonolysis proof: but-2-ene CH₃CH=CHCH₃ cleaves to 2×CH₃CHO; counting carbonyl fragments reconstructs the alkene skeleton (NEB 2022, 3 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Markovnikov predicts the MAJOR product — rearrangements (hydride/methyl shifts to stabler carbocations) rewrite outcomes. Free-radical halogenation of alkanes gives mixtures (selectivity 3° > 2° > 1° only biases). Wurtz fails for mixed R–R′ (statistical trio) and bulky halides (elimination wins).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: HX adds via protonation: H⁺ attacks the π bond forming the more substituted carbocation (hyperconjugation + inductive stabilisation scale with alkyl count), X⁻ then captures it — product distribution follows carbocation stability, hence Markovnikov. Peroxide flips the FIRST step to Br· radical addition, whose stability order reverses the outcome for HBr.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Addition of HX' → check symmetry first (symmetrical = one product, rule moot). Ozonolysis fragments: join carbonyl carbons back with C=C. Unsaturation tests: Br₂ water (brown→colourless) or Baeyer's (purple→brown MnO₂) — either proves π bonds.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): ethane from ethene + mechanism. NEB 2022 (3): but-2-ene ozonolysis — equations + products. Markovnikov/peroxide statements and alkyne acidity tests rotate yearly.
